subject: Amber20 sander speed difference between cmake and old configure method

messages.author: Charo del Genio
messages.body:
Dear all,
on my machine, sander from AmberTools20 run much slower when compiled using the cmake system versus the old configure script. In fact, on the same input, the speed is literally halved. I have tested
this fairly extensively, and I can exclude any effect due to choice of BLA vendor as well as system vs. bundled libraries (including all sort of combinations). At this stage, I really can't figure out
the origin of the problem. However, by comparing the output of ldd on the sander executables obtained with the two method, I notice that the cmake one links some libraries that are not found in the
"traditionally compiled" one. Specifically, these are
libfftw3
libemil
libsff_fortran
libnetcdff
libnetcdf
libarpack
liblapack
libblas
and their MPI versions, wherever appropriate. Am I right in assuming these are compiled in the traditional executable statically? If so, could this be the origin of the problem? If not, does anyone
have any idea of what causes it?
By the way, why doesn't libatlas get linked even though I explicitly set -DBLA_VENDOR=ATLAS?
Cheers,
Charo
--

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Wed, May 06, 2020, Charo del Genio wrote:
> on my machine, sander from AmberTools20 run much slower when compiled
> using the cmake system versus the old configure script.
Thanks for the report. It's possible that linking some shared libraries
(vs. loading static libs) could be the source, but that would be a
surprise, since none of those libraries is called much in a typical benchmark
calculation. FWIW, I don't see any speed difference between pmemd in
cmake vs legacy build -- don't know if you have tried that.
As far as I can see, the fortran optimization flags (-O3 -mtune_native)
are the same in the two builds, and I don't see obvious changes in the
link commands.
[I have just been running the "jac" benchmarks.]
....dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Wed, May 06, 2020, Charo del Genio wrote:
> on my machine, sander from AmberTools20 run much slower when compiled
> using the cmake system versus the old configure script.
To those who have already downloaded and installed AmberTools20: you
should consider using update_amber to install update.1 to fix the above
problem.
(If you haven't yet installed AmberTools20, the update will be
automatically incorporated into your build when to do so.)
Thanks to Charo del Genio for finding the problem and helping to fix it.
....dac
